_header.purpose: IAM resource-type family -> individual members, so a policy linter can expand `<verb> <family>` into the equivalent per-member statements.
_header.source: Hand-derived from research/04b-iam-security-cost-freetier.md §1-14 (§4 'Resource-types and family members'); generated 2026-09-08; verified-on CLI 3.91.0
rules: `<verb> <family>` is exactly equivalent to one statement per individual member.
A family silently widens: a new individual resource-type is folded into its service family automatically. Prefer individual resource-types in generated policy.
IAM has no family resource-type - only individual ones (see `no_family_individual_types`).
Some API operations need several resource-types at once (LaunchInstance = instances + network; CreateVolumeBackup = volumes + volume-backups); permissions are additive across groups.

Membership below is only what Oracle publishes verbatim in the Core Services / Object Storage policy reference. Families listed in `families_membership_not_enumerated` exist but their member lists are not reproduced here - read the per-service policy-reference page.

aggregates.all-resources: Every resource-type in the tenancy. Never generate it outside a deliberate admin or read-only-audit grant.

notes_on_members.instance-family.volume-attachments: Only the permissions needed to attach volumes; full volume-attachment control comes from volume-family.
notes_on_members.virtual-network-family: `inspect virtual-network-family` returns FULL security-list and route-table contents - it is not a metadata-only grant.

no_family_individual_types.note: IAM ships no family aggregate; write one statement per individual resource-type. The `iam` list is illustrative, not exhaustive - the source ends it with an ellipsis, so other IAM resource-types (e.g. `tag-defaults`, `authentication-policies`) exist; read the IAM policy-reference page.
